Hi. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the Q2 FY27 earnings call of Crompton Greaves 
Consumer Electricals Limited, hosted by Ambit Capital. 
Before we start, Crompton would like to point out that some of the statements made in today's

and analysts only. If there are representatives from the media, they are requested to kindly drop 
off this call immediately. 
Today, from the management side, we have with us Mr. Promeet Ghosh, Managing Director and 
Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Kaleeswaran Arunachalam, Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Sachin 
Phartiyal, Business Head, Home Electricals, Mr. Shaleen Nayak, Business Head, Lighting, Solar 
Rooftop and Wires, Mr. Anand Kumar, Business Head, Pumps and Kitchen Appliances, Mr. 
Rajat Chopra, Global Sales and Service Head, Ms. Shwetha Sagar, Chief Business Officer, 
Butterfly Gandhimathi, and Mr. Ruchir Jain, Head Investor Relations and Corporate Strategy.

raise hand feature to ask any questions post the opening remarks.  
Now, I invite Mr. Promeet Ghosh to take us through the key highlights of the quarter, post which 
we will open for Q&A. Thank you and over to you, Mr. Ghosh. 
Promeet Ghosh: 
Thank you, everyone. Thank you, Dhruv. And good evening, everyone. 
Welcome to the Crompton Greaves Q2 FY27 earnings call. We've also already uploaded the 
investor deck, so you would have had some detailed understanding of what we are doing. But 
nevertheless, I'll try and give you more colour as a part of this call. Also, thank you to the team 
at Ambit for hosting this call. My team here is joining me. Their names have already been 
introduced by Dhruv, so I'm not going to do it again. 
I'm very happy to share that Crompton's momentum of strong revenue growth and profit growth 
continues to strengthen. This is the third quarter of double-digit revenue growth and is 
accompanied by excellent profit growth. This progress has been driven by sustained brand 
building, relentless focus on innovation and excellence in execution. 
As a reflection of this transformation, in August 2026, we launched Crompton's refreshed brand 
identity featuring a new monogram, Cephyr, with a new tag and a distinctive sonic identity. 
Underpinning this evolution is our innovation agenda anchored in three strategic vectors: design-
led innovation, technology forward and smart & connected. By combining these three vectors 
across business units, we are continually developing and delivering industry-first products that 
translate into patents, awards, and most importantly, differentiated customer value. Now, coming 
to execution, to begin with, and this might be something that may be at the back of your minds, 
the supply chain disruptions which impacted us in Q1FY27 are behind us now. We have 
appropriately stepped-up inventory levels. 
Days of inventory which were low going into Q1FY27, as you will recall, have now normalized 
to similar levels as they were one year ago. Moving to our quarterly performance, the benefits 
of our efforts in repositioning the business are clearly visible. Crompton delivered robust double-

digit growth across all our business segments in Q2 FY27, driven by sharp and focused execution 
and meaningfully differentiated product launches, some of which, you can see in the investor 
deck.  
Amidst a challenging macro environment, our consolidated Q2 FY27 performance firmly 
validates the trajectory that we are on. Revenue grew by an impressive 18.2% YoY to Rs.2,263 
Crores. EBITDA delivered Rs.205 Crores, surging 24.1% YoY, with margins expanding 40 
basis points to 9% compared to a year ago. Operating leverage and Unnati programme drove the 
bottom-line growth in a tough macroeconomic environment with respect to commodities. PBT 
excluding exceptional items, grew by 36.2%. We had an exceptional item of Rs.20 Crores, as 
some of you will recall, in Q2 FY26, which was towards Baroda plant restructuring. This led to 
PAT growing at 65% ahead of PBT. PAT margins expanded by 160 basis points. This is not 
strictly comparable. The PBT number excluding exceptional is what is comparable. 
While we are very optimistic about our structural growth, we of course remain vigilant regarding 
macroeconomic headwinds. The industry is currently facing commodity cost pressures and 
unpredictable geopolitical developments. We have and are continuing to address these through 
disciplined combination of strategic price increases, consistent execution of Unnati cost savings 
and these are accompanying the benefits of operating leverage, which are showing in our 
business.  
As far as overall channel performance is concerned, general trade and rural trade, which are 
areas of particular strength of Crompton, both delivered double digit growth. E-commerce, 
however, was subdued on the back of efforts to reposition our go-to market in the e-commerce 
channel to improve channel profitability. You may recall that a similar exercise had been 
undertaken in Butterfly some quarters ago and is helping us handsomely in that business today.  
Now, coming to segment level performance. Our category leadership continues to be across our 
portfolio. In ECD, we delivered stellar 19.4% YoY growth with EBIT margins improving YoY 
to 11.6%. This is 30.7% growth over the previous year. Fans delivered double digit growth this 
quarter. Our BLDC fans continued the strong momentum, especially in general trade, with the 
growth of 40% aided by focused portfolio interventions and improved reach.  
Pumps - Our conventional pumps business, which includes residential, Agri and specialty 
pumps, delivered double digit growth. Solar pumps witnessed a slowdown as order inflow from 
Kusum 1.1, which is nearing completion, tapered. We are aware that this will pick up in the next 
quarter with GOI having announced Kusum 2.0. We expect the business to ramp up accordingly 
in the coming quarters. Solar pumps, importantly, continues to support our conventional Agri 
expansion, widening our distribution and portfolio range. This is aiding a strong trajectory in 
our agri business.  
Appliances - Large domestic appliances also grew at double digits, driven largely by water 
heaters. We continue to gain market share in our water heaters business during this quarter. 
Small domestic appliances also continued its momentum and grew yet again in excess of 20% 
this quarter, led by air fryers, induction cooktops and mixer grinders. The consistent 
improvement in top line in SDA is now translating into disproportionate growth in profitability.

As previously announced, we are restructuring our LKA business. As a part of the restructuring, 
going forward, both LKA and Rhion are being led by Shweta Sagar, the Chief Business Officer 
of Butterfly. Moreover, Rhion and LKA will leverage the broader Butterfly ecosystem. We 
expect this to materially reduce the overall cost structure and drive profitability in this segment.  
New businesses: 
Wires and Solar Rooftop: 
Wires and solar rooftop continue to build strong on-ground momentum. We launched our wires 
business in South India in Q1FY27 and based on positive early traction, we have now extended 
it to Punjab, Delhi NCR and Gujarat in the previous quarter. Our execution of solar pump is also 
stepping up strongly. We have executed more than 50% of our order book with the AP 
government. The business to consumer and commercial and industrial business of solar rooftop 
has also commenced in six states, and we are in the early stages of building this aspect of the 
business up.  
Lighting:  
Sustained performance with 14.3% YoY growth to Rs. 298 Crores. This has been driven by 
ceiling lights and outdoor range in B2C. This is something that I have been repeatedly calling 
out quarter after quarter. This is still the case here. Alongside this, industrial and indoor 
commercial segments are driving growth in B2B area. Both these segments that is industrial and 
indoor commercial segments have delivered strong double-digit growth this quarter. EBIT stood 
at 12.9% in lighting. It is lower than it was last year, largely due to the B2B business being 
impacted by pre-contracted orders.  
Butterfly:  
In Butterfly, mid-teens growth has sustained with 15.9% YoY growth. This is after excluding 
what was an in-house sale of mixer grinders, which was there in the base last year. This quarter 
is also marked with sustained revival across core categories in Butterfly as well as the retail sales 
channel. While the salience of cooktops has increased in Butterfly, a large bulk of the growth 
continues to be led by share gain in core categories. This is sustainable and high-quality growth 
as well as improvements in the share of premium portfolio in the sales of Butterfly.  
I am very happy to also report that our emphasis on developing international business is also 
beginning to bear fruit. Exports grew at more than 70% this quarter and recorded the highest 
ever quarterly revenues. We expect that the momentum in this channel will continue to build 
and it is our belief that international business presents a significant opportunity for this company 
over the next couple of years. Evaluation of Greenfield manufacturing plant is in advanced 
stages. With this, we expect to raise our manufacturing capabilities in fans, appliances, and 
wires. Looking ahead, having delivered consistent double-digit revenue and profit growth for 
the past three quarters on the back of various interventions in improving the quality of revenues 
and investing for the long term, we believe we are very well on track for our medium-term 
guidance. We are entering the second half of the year with tremendous momentum, a leaner cost 
structure, and a brand that is resonating deeply with consumers.
